title: From Data Localization to Digital Openness: Uzbekistan’s Regulatory Shift
author: Elnora Anvarova
text:
Head of the Uzbek Presidential Administration Saida Mirziyoyeva met recently with meeting with Vice President of Google Karan Bhatia for discussions on launching YouTube monetization in Uzbekistan.
Credit: Facebook / Saida Mirziyoyeva
During a visit to New York in late September, the head of Uzbekistan’s presidential administration, Saida Mirziyoyeva, met with Google Vice President Karan Bhatia to discuss the possibility of launching YouTube monetization in Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan has been actively seeking to expand its partnership with global digital companies in line with the country’s growing digital economy. Tashkent even re-wrote the laws that once made it difficult for international technology platforms to operate in the country. The 2021 amendment to Uzbekistan’s Law on Personal Data imposed a restriction on the storage and processing of Uzbek citizens’ data abroad, raising the question of how domestic regulation could accommodate services operating across borders. PayPal, Stripe, Netflix, Spotify, and Amazon Web Services refused to enter the Uzbek market while Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Google Cloud limited their functionality. [...]
